messages.subject: GGUM confirmatory
parts:
Hello group members

I am trying a multidimensional GGUM in my research that has about six factors and 47 items. I separated only two factors for testing, and it gives me the following factorial result



Items 1 - 5 are part of one factor and items 6 - 10 are another factor, so I tried the following confirmatory model.

modelo <-mirt.model('

F1 = 1-5

F2 = 6-10

COV=F1*F2')


ajuste3<-mirt(df6,itemtype='ggum',model = modelo, TOL=0.03)



The results apparently improved (i.e., closer to statistical significance), the IRT coefficients improved as well, but as the model is confirmatory, the values seems to be correct in the factors that they load at, but in the factor they do not load, the values should be zero, as the example shows bellow. Using the graded model, I receive sensible results, but with GGUM the results appear confounding.


ajuste3<-mirt(df6,model = modelo)




Sorry for my english, but I'm from brazil,

I would greatly appreciate if anyone could help me. Thank you in advance for your help.


--
Silvio
"A incerteza é o complemento do conhecimento."

Can you provide a reproducible example of this behaviour? It's possible this is a bug in the package given that the GGUM isn't one of the most commonly used IRT models that are fitted. Thanks.

Phil
